chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I wrote to him (peace be upon him) that a man sent a marriage proposal to his uncle for his daughter. So the uncle instructed one of his brothers to marry him the daughter who had been proposed for. The man erred regarding the name of the girl, so he named her with a name other than her actual name. Her name was Fatima, but he named her with a different name. There was no daughter of the man with the name that the spouse had mentioned. So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a marriage contract is made with an incorrect name for the bride?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the flexibility in marriage contracts (*nikah*) when the essential identity of the bride is clear, even if a specific attribute like her name is mistaken. It highlights the practical wisdom of the Imams in avoiding the invalidation of unions due to minor clerical or verbal errors, provided there is no ambiguity regarding the person. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the validity of contracts based on substantial intent rather than rigid formalism.
